review.summary: Phase 90's deliverable — the G10 0.1.1 plan, the governance tooling that will gate phase 91, and an honest pinned-branch assessment — meets its acceptance criteria with source-bound, independently checkable evidence, and every finding from attempts 01-03 is genuinely closed. The executed gate is real and complete: docs/checks/phase-90.json records exactly the seven commands of commands_for(90) (tools/check_phase.py:71-80) in order, all integer exit_code 0, timeout false, bound to source_sha256 b04b72796126… equal to the reviewed fingerprint, source_unchanged true; recorded stderr shows 29 review-gate and 26 CI governance tests OK. The private-material receipt is a freshly executed scan, not a replay: docs/checks/phase-90-private-material.json:3-8 records 13:22:51Z against the same fingerprint and headCommit a6d63e58, five seconds before the gate's 13:22:56, passed true, 1356 files, 0 credential matches, 124 packaged candidates with 0 registration-value matches, 0 new/changed tenant occurrences, and scripts/check-private-material.py:155-176 recomputes both the source-only and packaged fingerprints and rejects any receipt that is not a successful scan. Attempt-03's blocking medium — the false review_dispositions ledger — is fixed properly: docs/phase-status.json:1831-2038 now carries 22 per-finding review_fixes entries, exactly covering attempt-01's 8, attempt-02's 7 and attempt-03's 7 findings, each with a resolvable `source` pointer and specific acceptance_evidence, plus preserved_checks for all three attempt reports. I verified roughly a dozen of those pointers rather than trusting them: tools/check_phase.py:73 really is `840c090..HEAD`; tools/check_phase.py:96-98 really adds generate_constants/verify_gateway_bindings/model_fixtures and :86-90 the five previously missing governance suites; docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:12-16 really cites STABILITY.md's patch rule, :84-95 really requires the README/RELEASE/STABILITY current-version statements, tools/test_g10_release.py and the full package delta, and :219-222 really marks the token-authorization edits as completed in phase 90. Attempt-03's unsupported-reproduction low is closed with an actual executed receipt (docs/checks/g10-pre-fix-copy-limit-reproduction.json) whose byte arithmetic is self-consistent with the defect. Historical baseline command sets are intact: I recomputed commands_for(8) by hand through the 1→3→4→5→6→7→8 chain and it yields 77 commands, matching the 77 recorded in docs/checks/phase-08.json, and tools/test_review_phase.py:20-24 now pins phases 1-8 by hash. The gate mechanics added here do not weaken the gate: require_nonempty_tests (check_phase.py:23-39) fails before any subprocess so the not-yet-written tools/test_g10_release.py slot cannot record a vacuous pass, next_phase (review_phase.py:156-158) takes the smallest greater id so 8→90→91 cannot skip a gate, and validate_predecessors still re-verifies every lower-id phase's accepted review. I independently confirmed the plan's compatibility contract against the pinned code: Mode stays #[non_exhaustive] (validation.rs:13-27), RequestOptions has no Default impl so with_timeout is the only constructor and always sets response_defaults: true (config.rs:367-381), root-level omission really is suppressed at validation.rs:372-376 so docs/VALIDATION.md's parse_optional claim holds, response_mode() reaches exactly the buffered one-of, buffered single-contract and SSE contract paths (engine.rs:643, :721, streaming.rs:113) with realtime deliberately unaffected, generated newtype Mode::Response uses are scalar contracts with no defaults, and defaulted fields use Optional/Patch presence wrappers with skip-if-unset serialization (generated.rs:12139-12200), so the typed omission contract is structurally achievable. The copy-budget defect is confirmed in source (validation.rs:766-771: copy_text(key) runs only inside the insertion body) and is correctly booked as phase-91 work that blocks publication. What remains are lows and one deferred medium: the unconditional acceptance-parity text still ships in committed public rustdoc, VALIDATION.md and the Unreleased changelog while a counterexample is proven; the review_fixes scope strings are truncated mid-path; the planned contracts/response-defaults.json sidecar has no named verifying command in the phase-91 set; and the pinned-commit identity is prose only. None of these is a high or blocker, no credential exposure exists, and nothing is published.

findings.description: The unconditional acceptance-parity claim ships in four places in the reviewed source while a counterexample is proven by this phase's own executed receipt. CHANGELOG.md:12 states "Acceptance is identical to the default policy"; the public rustdoc at crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:20-23 states Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults accepts and rejects "exactly the same documents"; the public rustdoc at crates/scm-sdk/src/config.rs:399-401 repeats it for without_response_defaults; docs/VALIDATION.md:20-21 repeats it again; and the in-source comment at validation.rs:764-765 asserts "acceptance never depends on whether defaults are materialized". All five are false: at validation.rs:766-771 `self.copy_text(key)?` executes only inside the insertion body, so under Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults a suppressed default's key bytes are never charged against max_copied_bytes. docs/checks/g10-pre-fix-copy-limit-reproduction.json:21-25 is an executed Rust 1.89 reproduction bound to this exact source (sourceSha256 b04b7279…) showing Response rejects with Err(Limit) and ResponseWithoutDefaults accepts the same document under identical limits; the 42-vs-23-byte difference equals len("basic_auth_location"), which is exactly the suppressed key. This is not a phase-90 blocker: the phase forbids SDK fixes before the plan gate (docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:50-51), the defect is booked as phase-91 work (plan:62-66, :75-77), publication is explicitly blocked on it (plan:164-170), and the ledger records it as deferred_to_phase_91_blocks_publication three times (docs/phase-status.json:1878-1886, 1923-1932, 2005-2014). It remains a demonstrably false invariant living in committed public API documentation with no test pinning it.
findings.required_fix: In phase 91, charge the omitted default key's copy/work budget identically before deciding whether to insert it (crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:766-771), and add a public-boundary regression test pinning equal copy accounting between Mode::Response and Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults at the max_copied_bytes boundary, using the document and limits recorded in docs/checks/g10-pre-fix-copy-limit-reproduction.json, before any of the four unconditional statements ships in a published artifact. Do not tag or publish 0.1.1 while the text and the code disagree.

findings.description: The new per-finding review_fixes ledger is accurate and its `source` pointers resolve exactly, but every `scope` string is truncated mid-token, apparently by splitting the original finding text on the first period: line 1835 reads "Phase 90's edit to docs/phase-status" (cut inside the filename), line 1844 ends at "-p test_g10_release", line 1853 ends at "`args", line 1862 ends at "release-registry-0", line 1899 ends at "docs/VALIDATION", line 1908 ends at "qualified 0", line 1936 ends at "tools/check_phase", line 1945 ends at "`git diff --check 840c090", line 1963 ends at "rather than 0", line 1990 ends at "wrong at 0", line 2018 ends at "docs/RELEASE", line 2027 ends at "on Rust 1". Attempt-03's medium required replacing boilerplate with per-finding detail; the resolutions and evidence now satisfy that, but the scope column is no longer readable as a standalone record of what was found, which is the column a future maintainer reads first.
findings.required_fix: Rewrite each review_fixes[].scope as a complete short sentence (or truncate on a whitespace boundary with an explicit ellipsis) so no entry ends inside a path, flag or version number, keeping the existing `source`, `resolution` and `acceptance_evidence` fields unchanged.

findings.description: Plan step 91.5 requires recording "the three additive Rust APIs and all 23 default bindings in a separate `contracts/response-defaults.json` sidecar, checked against frozen sources and executable Rust tests", but no command in commands_for(91) (tools/check_phase.py:81-125) names that sidecar, and no generator with a `--check` mode is assigned to it. The other generated ledgers each have an explicit verifying command (native_operations.py --check at :102, native_exports.py --check at :103, verify_gateway_bindings.py --check at :97, model_fixtures.py --check at :98), so the sidecar is the only planned artifact whose determinism check is unassigned. The implied owner is tools/test_g10_release.py (plan:116-117), but the plan only charges that suite with the current-version statements, so a hand-edited or stale sidecar could pass the phase-91 gate.
findings.required_fix: State in plan step 91.5 which command verifies contracts/response-defaults.json against the frozen semantics and the Rust source (for example an assertion in tools/test_g10_release.py, or a dedicated generator with --check added to commands_for(91)), and ensure that command is present in the phase-91 set before the gate is run.

findings.description: The phase record pins the reviewed input as source_branch "g10-no-response-defaults" and source_commit "a6d63e58f067a98504e5b79987639d53e11fc931", and docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:5-8 repeats the pin, but nothing executable asserts it. The working branch is release/0.1.1, not the named branch; commands_for(90) line 73 now uses `840c090..HEAD` (which correctly follows the branch rather than assuming the pin), and scripts/check-private-material.py:174-175 validates only the format of the recorded headCommit, not equality with a6d63e5. The private receipt happens to record headCommit a6d63e58, so the pin is corroborated for this run, but it is corroboration by coincidence rather than by assertion: a future phase-90 re-run on a different HEAD would still pass every command while the record continued to claim a6d63e5.
findings.required_fix: Either add a governance unit test (tools/test_review_phase.py or tools/test_ci.py) asserting that docs/phase-status.json's phase-90 source_commit equals the headCommit recorded in docs/checks/phase-90-private-material.json, or record the actual working branch alongside the supplied branch name in scope_evidence so the record cannot drift from the checkout it describes.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-90.json:7-154 records exactly the seven commands of tools/check_phase.py:71-80 in the same order (840c090..HEAD whitespace, working-tree whitespace, staged whitespace, test_review_phase.py, test_ci.py, verify-contracts.py, check-private-material.py --check docs/checks/phase-90-private-material.json), each with integer exit_code 0 and timeout false, with phase 90, passed true, source_unchanged true and source_sha256 b04b72796126624d3c81d8f3e3e11380bffa44eb42a677fa3fe0e4e0a28c4dbe equal to the reviewed fingerprint in my prompt. Recorded stderr shows 29 review-gate tests and 26 CI governance tests OK, including test_discovery_rejects_missing_and_empty_suites, test_noncontiguous_maintenance_successors and test_historical_phase_command_contracts_are_unchanged.

The private-material evidence is a fresh executed scan bound to this source: docs/checks/phase-90-private-material.json:3-8 records checkedAt 2026-10-18T13:22:51Z, sourceSha256 b04b7279… (identical to the reviewed fingerprint), headCommit a6d63e58…, sourceUnchanged true, passed true, 1356 Git-visible files, 0 selectedExternalClientIdentityOrSecretMatches, 124 packaged candidates with 0 publishedCrateSourceOrExampleRegistrationValueMatches and existingTenantIdentifier.newOrChangedFilesCount 0 with matchingFilesCount == alreadyPresentInHeadFilesCount == 3, five seconds before the gate's checked_at 13:22:56 (docs/checks/phase-90.json:5). scripts/check-private-material.py:144-176 rejects any receipt that is not a successful scan and recomputes both the source-only and packaged-candidate fingerprints, and scripts/evidence_common.py:194-200 shows source_fingerprint excludes docs/reviews/, docs/checks/ and docs/phase-status.json in both modes, so the two fingerprints are comparable.

Historical baseline command sets are intact, verified by independent recomputation rather than by the new hash pin alone: counting commands_for(1)=7, (3)=26, (4)=29, (5)=33, (6)=36, (7)=48, (8)=77 through tools/check_phase.py:126-275 yields exactly the 77 `"command": [` entries in docs/checks/phase-08.json, which matches the 77 qualification commands recorded for the accepted phase-8 gate (docs/phase-status.json:649). tools/test_review_phase.py:20-24 additionally pins commands_for(1..8) by SHA-256.

The review-disposition ledger is now complete and accurate. docs/reviews/phase-90-attempt-01.json has 8 findings, attempt-02 has 7 and attempt-03 has 7; docs/phase-status.json:1831-2033 contains exactly 22 review_fixes entries keyed as `docs/reviews/phase-90-attempt-NN.json:review.findings[i]` covering all of them, with docs/phase-status.json:2034-2038 listing the three preserved check reports that attempt-02 finding 2 required. I resolved the evidence pointers rather than trusting them: tools/check_phase.py:73 is `["git","diff","--check","840c090..HEAD"]`; tools/check_phase.py:96-98 adds generate_constants.py --check, verify_gateway_bindings.py --check and model_fixtures.py --check; tools/check_phase.py:86-90 adds test_model_fixtures, test_model_generation, test_native_fixtures, test_verify_gateway_bindings and test_auxiliary_evidence; tools/test_ci.py:213-215 builds `publications` from every phase carrying registry_publication and takes the last; docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:12-16 cites STABILITY.md's patch rule; :84-95 requires the README/RELEASE/STABILITY current-version statements, tools/test_g10_release.py and the complete packaged-file delta; :219-222 marks the token-authorization edits as completed in phase 90.

Attempt-03's unsupported-execution low is closed with an actual receipt: docs/checks/g10-pre-fix-copy-limit-reproduction.json:4-25 records checkedAt 13:22:50Z, sourceCommit a6d63e58…, sourceSha256 b04b7279… (the reviewed source), the exact cargo +1.89.0 --locked --offline command, the rustc 1.89.0 banner, the full manifest and program source, exitCode 0 and stdout `Response: Err(Limit)` / `ResponseWithoutDefaults: Ok("accepted")`. The arithmetic is self-consistent with the source defect: the Spec report's 42-vs-23 byte difference is 19 = len("basic_auth_location"), exactly the key whose copy_text is skipped at crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:770, and docs/reviews/g10-pinned-branch-independent-review.md:11-13 now links the receipt and states it demonstrates a known defect rather than qualifying a release.

The compatibility contract in docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:23-43 matches the pinned code by inspection: crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:13-27 keeps Mode #[non_exhaustive] and adds ResponseWithoutDefaults with is_response()/inserts_defaults() predicates; crates/scm-sdk/src/config.rs:361-381 shows RequestOptions has private fields and no Default impl, so with_timeout is the only constructor and always sets response_defaults: true; :406-413 are the two additive methods and :414-430 the feature-gated response_mode(); validation.rs:525-530 still substitutes the schema default into the walk so an absent defaulted value is validated before being discarded at :766-771; validation.rs:372-376 suppresses a root-level default for parse_optional, which is the behavior docs/VALIDATION.md:22-24 claims.

Propagation is exactly where the plan says it is and nowhere else: `response_mode()` appears at crates/scm-sdk/src/engine.rs:643 (parse_one_of_with_limits for alternative contracts), engine.rs:721 (normalize_contract for buffered single-schema responses) and crates/scm-sdk/src/streaming.rs:113 (SSE contract events). crates/scm-sdk/src/realtime/mod.rs:330 deliberately keeps Mode::Response, matching docs/VALIDATION.md:30, and the remaining hardcoded Mode::Response uses in crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs are scalar newtype validators (for example :8039-8048) with no object keys or defaults.

The typed omission contract is structurally achievable on the pinned branch: defaulted fields use presence wrappers with skip-if-unset serialization, e.g. crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs:12139-12140 declares `ws_response_timeout: Optional<FiniteNumber>` with `#[serde(default)]` and :12198-12200 emits it only when `!is_unset()`, so a suppressed default stays absent in the reserialized document rather than failing decode.

The gate mechanics added in this phase do not weaken it: tools/check_phase.py:23-39 raises on countTestCases()==0 and converts that to exit_code 1 before any subprocess starts, with reject and accept cases at tools/test_review_phase.py:32-48, so the not-yet-written tools/test_g10_release.py slot in commands_for(91) cannot record a vacuous pass; tools/review_phase.py:156-158 returns the smallest greater phase id (asserted for 8->90->91->None at test_review_phase.py:26-30) so maintenance numbering cannot skip a gate; review_phase.py:99-113 accepts a check report only on exact command-list equality with commands_for(phase) plus passed/source equality; :116-142 binds reviewer, gate_passed, prompt and CLI hashes, CLI structured_output equality and the checks digest; :145-153 re-verifies every lower-id phase's accepted review; :92 requires score >= 9 with no blocker/high.

Documentation continuity is consistent and does not overclaim: docs/CI.md:10-12 states that the maintenance plan replaces the Phase 8 CI invocation with the Phase 91 gate and that the two tools/test_ci.py assertions change together, while docs/CI.md:104 still accurately describes the current `--phase 8 --verification-only` job; docs/RELEASE.md:24-28 routes 0.1.1 through gates 90 then 91 and states Phase 8's historical receipts do not qualify changed 0.1.1 inputs; docs/RELEASE.md:3-13 keeps the 0.1.0 facts that phase 91 will update; docs/implementation-plan.md:127 records the owner-controlled token mechanism and points at the plan; docs/PHASES.md:19-24 adds rows 90/91 and states the maintenance track follows the eight baseline phases. docs/RELEASE.md:65-69 already documents the ignored .local proof path plus later evidence-only retention, so the plan's .local-to-docs/checks receipt handling follows an established convention.
limitations: Read-only Read/Glob/Grep with no command execution: I could not recompute the reviewed fingerprint b04b7279…, the docs/checks/phase-90.json digest a0c11f8d… quoted in my prompt, or the private-material receipt's recomputed fingerprints, and I could not run tools/test_ci.py or tools/test_review_phase.py. I verified recorded exit codes, exact command-list equality against commands_for(90), and the fix logic by reading code; the test results are the gate's recorded evidence, not my own execution.

tools/review_phase.py:43-60 and scripts/evidence_common.py:194-200 exclude docs/phase-status.json, docs/reviews/ and docs/checks/ from the source fingerprint, so this phase's status-file deliverables (scope_evidence and the 22-entry review_fixes ledger) and the preserved check reports sit outside the binding of both the executed gate and the private scan. I assessed them by direct reading; I cannot tell from the artifacts whether they were written before or after the 13:22:56 check, and nothing would detect a later edit.

The phase-90 gate executes no Rust, generator, export, package, dependency or cross-compile command, so every runtime claim about the pinned branch — compilation and clippy across the feature sets, the new red_team target test passing, SSE/buffered propagation at runtime — is unexecuted in this phase. My propagation, presence-wrapper and root-suppression conclusions are from source inspection. This is the phase's declared scope (docs/PHASES.md:19, docs/phase-status.json:1808), not a concealed gap.

I could not run git, so I could not diff tools/check_phase.py, tools/review_phase.py, tools/test_ci.py, tools/test_review_phase.py or the changed documents against their pre-phase state, and I could not confirm that HEAD equals the pinned a6d63e5 beyond the headCommit recorded in docs/checks/phase-90-private-material.json:5 and the session's commit context. My conclusion that historical command sets are unchanged rests on recomputing commands_for(8) and matching it to the 77 commands in docs/checks/phase-08.json, not on a diff.

I sampled rather than exhaustively resolved the 23 ZodDefault bindings in contracts/native-semantics.json (I confirmed the count is exactly 23) and their owning wrapper chains, and I checked one defaulted field's generated presence wrapper rather than all of them. An acceptance or roundtrip difference arising from some other effect, refinement or union path is not fully excluded; the plan's all-23 inventory and regression requirement remains the right control.
I verified roughly twelve of the 22 review_fixes evidence pointers by opening the cited file and line; the remainder I checked only for internal consistency against the attempt reports.

I read no credential or tenant-registration material, nothing outside this repository, and made no network calls. The plan's live-qualification, tag, push and crates.io steps are judged purely as written text; none has been executed in this phase, and nothing is published beyond the historical 0.1.0 artifact.
